To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the levels of capsinoids and other bioactives in pepper cultivars were influenced by the stage of ripening and cooking method.
the capsaicin content of the peppers ranged from non-detectable to 4820 μg/g.
the levels of bioactive compounds and antioxidant activities in peppers depend on the cultivar, stage of maturity, and cooking methods.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the capsaicin content and other bioactive constituents in different cultivars of Capsicum annuun at both the mature and red/yellow stages.
the identification of bioactive compounds in peppers, which are important to the human health and the development of new functional foods.
the identification and characterization of the capsaicin and capsaicin derivatives in different cultivars of Capsicum annuam at both the mature and red stages and the effect of roasting.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
roasting peppers increases capsaicin content, but decreases ascorbic acid content and antioxidant activity, whereas total phenolic and flavonoid contents increased after roasting.
the levels of capsinoid, polyphenol, and antioxidant activities in the mature red stage were higher than those of the mature green stage.
the content of capsaicoids and other bioactives compounds, such as phenolics, flavonoids and ascorbic acid varied among the different pepper cultivars.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
peppers are an excellent source of bioactive compounds and antioxidants.
the red/yellow mature peppers have higher capsaicin and dihydrocapsaicins, total phenolics, flavonoids, antioxidant activities, and ascorbic acid than mature green peppers.
the levels of capsiate, capsaicin, dihydrocapsaicine and other bioactive components varied in different pepper varieties.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the nutritional value and bioactivity of peppers are affected by ripening stage and cooking methods, and these factors should be considered when selecting peppers for consumption.
the levels of bioactive compounds in the mature green or red/yellow stages of peppers depend on the pepper cultivar and that roasting affects their content and antioxidant activities.
the content of the different phytochemicals varies depending on the pepper variety and the stage of ripeness.
